set.st: James Ford, back from California c.1858, buried about $1,500 in gold in a field in the Town of Franklin and could not find it again. In Sept 1875, after his death, his brother John's hired man found a $20 gold piece among some stones and five more double eagles turned up ($120); the family was still hunting the remaining $1,380. Plow-scattered: grid the field with a detector. Private: permission.

src: Evening Wisconsin, via Wisconsin State Journal, 29 Sep 1875

set.pl: Near Carney, Menominee County; farm not yet located
set.tovw: Lead grade C: single source (treasure thread)
set.st: Ole Johnson of Carney, charged in 1906 with a 1901 murder (dismissed May 1906), was said by his wife in her divorce suit to have money hidden all over his farm; he once lifted stones from a stone pile and took out a salmon can full of $10 gold pieces. Farm near Carney not yet located.
pinev: Town-level: placed at Carney; the farm is not yet located (about 5 km).
